summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, seizure disorder, diabetes, and bipolar disorder was admitted after experiencing a seizure en route to the hospital for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He had recently undergone stent placement and reported no improvement. Labs showed leukocytosis, low antiepileptic drug levels, and metabolic acidosis, which resolved with IV fluids. CT confirmed acute on chronic pancreatitis with peripancreatic stranding. The pancreatic stent was removed via ERCP due to persistent symptoms. His pain improved, he was advanced to a full diet, and his seizure medications were adjusted. A rash and enlarged lymph node behind the ear were noted; he was treated with topical steroids and a course of dicloxacillin for possible cellulitis. He was discharged home in good condition, tolerating oral intake, with instructions to follow up on his pancreas condition, lymph node, and medications.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
